title: Expected and relative frequency
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:55Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point teaches both relative frequency and expected frequency together, but neither bank point covers both: each teaches only one idea, and both are written at Year 12 depth rather than Year 7.

draft.title: Expected and relative frequency
card: Relative frequency
how often an event happened in an experiment, divided by the number of trials. It can be written as a fraction, decimal or percentage.
Expected frequency
the number of times you expect an event to happen. Expected frequency = probability × number of trials.
Example
Sam spins a spinner 50 times and gets red 12 times. The relative frequency of red is 12/50 = 0.24.
Example
If the probability of red is 1/4, the expected frequency in 200 spins is 1/4 × 200 = 50. The real count may be different from this.
draft.remember: Relative frequency comes from results. Expected frequency comes from probability.

a.q: Priya flips a coin 40 times and gets heads 18 times. What is the relative frequency of heads?
a.why: Relative frequency is the number of heads divided by the number of trials: 18 ÷ 40. Using 22 divides by the number of tails, which is not the number of trials.
a.clue: Divide by the total number of flips.

b.q: A fair six-sided die is rolled 120 times. How many times is a number greater than 4 expected?
b.why: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3. Expected frequency = 1/3 × 120 = 40. The answer 20 comes from counting only the 5, which is 1/6 × 120.
b.clue: Count the outcomes greater than 4, not including 4.

final.title: Expected and relative frequency
card: Relative frequency

Expected frequency
the number of times you expect an event to happen. Expected frequency \(=\) probability \(\times\) number of trials.
Example
Sam spins a spinner 50 times and gets red 12 times. The relative frequency of red is \(\frac{12}{50} = 0.24\).
Example
If the probability of red is \(\frac{1}{4}\), the expected frequency in 200 spins is \(\frac{1}{4} \times 200 = 50\). The real count may be different from this.
